Jewelry noun (귀 + 걸이 = earrings); takes specific verb 하다 or 끼다 (귀걸이를 하다/끼다).
Jewelry noun (목 + 걸이 = necklace); takes wearable verb 하다 or 걸다 (목걸이를 하다/걸다).
Jewelry noun (斑指 = finger ring); selectional restriction: takes wearable verb 끼다 (반지를 끼다/빼다); counter: 개.
Joseon royal palace proper noun (景福宮 = main royal palace in Seoul); locative -에서 (경복궁을 관람하다, 수문장 교대의식).
Juice loanword; counters are 잔 (glass) and 병 (bottle). Collocates with 마시다.
Kinship noun ('eldest/older paternal uncle' = father's older brother); wife is 큰어머니; contrast with 작은아버지 (father's married younger brother) and 삼촌 (unmarried).
Kinship noun ('nephew / niece' = sibling's child); non-gendered in Korean unless specified (조카딸 = niece, 조카 = nephew/general).
Kinship noun (wife of father's older brother 큰아버지).
Kinship noun (外 + 할머니 = maternal grandmother); takes honorific particles -께서/-께 and honorific verb forms (진지, 주무시다, 계시다).
Kinship noun (外 + 할아버지 = maternal grandfather); takes honorific particles -께서/-께 and honorific predicates.
Kinship noun (外三寸 = maternal uncle / mother's brother); wife is 외숙모 (外叔母).
Kinship noun (外叔母 = wife of maternal uncle 외삼촌).
Kinship noun (姑母夫 = husband of paternal aunt 고모); addressed politely as 고모부 / 고모부님.
Kinship noun (姨母 = mother's sister / maternal aunt; husband is 이모부); also colloquial friendly address for female restaurant staff.
Kinship noun (姨母夫 = husband of maternal aunt 이모).
Kinship noun (親戚 = relatives/extended family); collocates with 친척 집, 친척들을 만나다.
Kinship noun; formal/in-law honorific is 아버님, colloquial is 아빠. Requires subject honorific marking (아버지께서).
Kinship noun; formal/in-law honorific is 어머님, colloquial is 엄마. Requires subject honorific marking (어머니께서).

Kinship term (작은어머니 = aunt, specifically the wife of father's married younger brother [작은아버지]); kinship address and reference; vocative 작은어머니; respectful reference; contrast with 큰어머니 (wife of father's older brother), 이모 (maternal aunt), 고모 (paternal aunt).
Kinship term used strictly by female speaker for older female sibling; contrasts with 누나 (male speaker).
Kinship term used strictly by female speaker for older male sibling/friend; contrasts with 형 (male speaker).
Kinship term used strictly by male speaker for older female sibling; contrasts with 언니 (female speaker). Respectful form 누님.
Kinship term used strictly by male speaker for older male sibling; contrasts with 오빠 (female speaker). Respectful form 형님.
Kitchen goods compound noun (廚房用品 = kitchenware / cookware / kitchen utensils); collocates with 주방용품 코너.
Korean currency unit; strictly requires Sino-Korean numbers (천 원, 만 원).
Korean Lunar New Year holiday; pronounced [설랄] via liquidization (유음화). Collocates with 세배하다, 떡국, 한복.
Labor income noun (月給 = monthly salary); collocates with 월급을 받다/타다, 첫 월급, 월급날.
Landscape aesthetic noun (風景 = natural scenery / vista / landscape); collocations: 풍경이 아름답다 / 그림 같다 (scenery is picturesque), 시골 풍경 (rural scenery).
Language noun (日本語 = Japanese language); collocations: 일본어를 배우다 / 공부하다 / 말하다 (learn/study/speak Japanese), 일본어과 (Japanese language department); synonym 일본말.
Language noun (韓國語 = Korean language); collocations: 한국어를 배우다 / 공부하다 / 가르치다 (learn/study/teach Korean), 한국어를 하다 / 잘하다 (speak Korean well), 한국어 수업 (Korean class); synonym 한국말.
Left direction noun; antonym of 오른쪽. Takes directional particle -으로 (왼쪽으로 가세요 = go left).
Legal/business verb (契約 + 하다); takes object with -을/를 (집을 계약하다, 방을 계약하다); partner with -와/과 계약하다.
Leisure noun (趣味 = hobby / pastime / interest); collocations: 취미가 뭐예요? (what is your hobby?), 취미 생활 (hobby life), 취미로 하다 (do as a hobby), 다양한 취미 (diverse hobbies).
Lending compound verb (빌리다 + 주다 = to lend / loan something to someone); takes object with -을/를 and recipient with -에게/-한테 (친구에게 돈을 빌려주다); antonym is 빌리다 (borrow).
Length/duration adjective; antonym of 길다. Double batchim ㄼ pronounced [짤따] / [짤바요].
Light verb construction (요리 + 를 + 하다); can take specific food/dish with modifier (한국 요리를 하다).
Light verb construction; takes comitative partner with -와/과, -하고, or -(이)랑 (친구와 약속을 하다).
Linguistic pedagogical noun (ㅅ-irregular verbs); describes verbs ending in ㅅ that drop ㅅ before vowel-initial suffixes (낫다, 붓다, 짓다, 잇다, 젓다, 긋다) while regular verbs retain it (씻다, 벗다, 빗다).
Lipid noun ('oil / grease / gasoline'); collocates with 기름을 두르다 (coat pan with oil), 참기름 (sesame oil), 기름을 넣다 (pump gas).
Loanword noun ('roller coaster'); takes accusative -를 with 타다 (롤러코스터를 타다 = ride a roller coaster).
Loanword noun ('roommate'); collocates with 룸메이트를 구하다 (look for a roommate), 룸메이트와 살다.
Loanword noun (aesthetic design / styling); collocations: 디자인이 예쁘다 / 독특하다, 디자인을 전공하다 (major in design), 패션 디자인.
Loanword noun (homepage / website); collocates with 홈페이지에 들어가다 / 접속하다 (access website) or 홈페이지에서 확인하다.
Loanword noun: (1) hospitality / customer service; (2) complimentary food/perk on the house (이거 서비스예요 = this is on the house, 서비스로 드리다).
Locational noun (洞네 = neighborhood / local residential area); collocates with 우리 동네, 동네 주민, 동네 한 바퀴.
Locative collocation: takes place + 에/에서 (서울에 살다)
Locative destination particle (-에다가, emphatic/colloquial variant of -에); marks surface or container receiving object (공책에다가 쓰다, 냉장고에다가 넣다).
Lodging loanword (hostel/guesthouse); takes locative -에서 with 묵다 and 예약하다.
Long-form post-verbal auxiliary negation: attaches to verb/adjective stem
Luggage noun (背囊 = backpack / knapsack); selectional restriction: takes verb 메다 (배낭을 메다); collocates with 배낭여행.
Lunar calendar noun (陰曆); pronounced [음녁] via nasalization. Contrasts with 양력 (solar calendar).
Magazine publisher workplace (雜誌社); takes allative -에 with 다니다.
Manner adverb ('diligently / hard'); modifies active verbs (열심히 공부하다, 열심히 일하다, 열심히 살다).
Manner adverb ('separately / apart / independently'); modifies predicates (따로 계산하다 = pay separately, 따로 살다 = live apart).
Manner adverb ('slowly / unhurriedly'); antonym of 빨리. Modifies speech, motion, actions (천천히 말해주세요, 천천히 걸어요).
Manner adverb ('suddenly / abruptly / out of the blue'); modifies sudden onset actions or changes of state (갑자기 비가 오다, 갑자기 생각이 나다).

Manner adverb (仔細히 = in detail / thoroughly / closely); modifies perception and communication verbs (자세히 보다 = look closely, 자세히 설명하다 = explain in detail, 자세히 알다 / 조사하다); derived from descriptive 자세하다.
Manner adverb (直接 = directly / personally / in person / firsthand); antonym 간접적(으로); premodifies action verbs (직접 가다, 직접 확인하다, 직접 요리하다).

Manner adverb expressing deep/complete state (soundly / thoroughly / completely); strongly collocates with rest and recuperation predicates: 푹 쉬세요 (get plenty of rest), 푹 자다, 푹 끓이다 (simmer thoroughly).
Maternal grandfather (외- prefix); requires subject honorifics (외할아버지께서).
Maternal grandmother (외- prefix); requires subject honorifics (외할머니께서 진지를 드시다).
Measurement compound noun (몸 + 무게 = body weight); collocations: 몸무게를 재다 (weigh oneself), 몸무게가 늘다 / 빠지다 (gain/lose weight); Sino-Korean synonym 체중.
Measurement loanword noun ('size'); collocates with 사이즈가 맞다/크다/작다, 무슨 사이즈.
Measurement noun (weight / heaviness); collocates with 무게를 달다 / 재다 (weigh / measure weight), 무게가 나가다 / 무겁다 (be heavy).
Measurement noun (速度 = speed / velocity); collocates with 속도가 빠르다 / 느리다, 속도를 줄이다 (reduce speed) / 내다 (speed up), 인터넷 속도.
Measurement noun derived from 길다 (length / extent); collocates with 길이를 재다 (measure length), 길이가 길다 / 짧다.
Measurement noun derived from 높다 (height / altitude); also functions as manner adverb ('high / highly'); noun collocates with 높이를 재다 (measure height), 높이가 높다.
Measurement noun nominalized from 크다 (size / dimensions); collocates with 크기가 크다 / 작다, 크기를 재다 / 비교하다.
Mechanical/electronic loanword noun ('button / push-button'); counter: 개; collocates with 버튼을 누르다 (press button).
Media broadcast noun; collocates with 보다 (드라마를 보다). Counter for series/episodes is 편.

Media communication noun (放送 = broadcasting / broadcast / telecast); collocations: 방송을 보다 / 듣다 (watch/listen to broadcast), 방송국 (broadcasting station), 텔레비전/라디오 방송, 생방송 (live broadcast); forms transitive/intransitive 방송하다.
Media loanword noun ('photo album / music album'); counter: 장; collocates with 사진 앨범, 앨범을 넘기다.
Medial demonstrative place pronoun ('there' / near listener); takes locative particles (거기에, 거기서).
Medial directional noun ('that way / your side'); can also function colloquially as a 2nd person reference ('your side / you').

Medial/anaphoric demonstrative determiner (그 = that / the); prenominal modifier preceding noun: 그 사람 (that person), 그 책 (that book); refers to entities close to listener or previously mentioned discourse referents.
Medical abnormality noun (異常 = health anomaly / abnormality / symptom); collocations: 몸에 이상이 생기다 / 있다 (something is wrong with body), 이상 증상 (abnormal symptoms).
Medical activity noun (治療 = medical treatment / cure); forms active 치료하다 (to treat) and passive 치료받다 (receive treatment); collocations: 물리 치료 (physical therapy), 치과 치료.
Medical facility; pairs with 아프다 (when ill) and directional 가다 (병원에 가다 = go to the doctor).
Medical gastrointestinal noun (便秘 = constipation); collocations: 변비에 걸리다 / 변비가 심하다, 변비약 (laxative).
Medicine noun (藥); strictly takes verb 먹다 (약을 먹다 = take medicine). Homonym with adverbial approximation 약 (約 = approximately).
Meteorological accumulation verb taking subject -이/가 (안개가 끼다 = fog gathers/settles, 구름이 끼다, 먼지가 끼다); conjugates 껴요 / 껴서 / 낍니다.
Meteorological descriptive adjective (濕하다 = to be humid / damp / clammy); stem 습하- -> 습해요 / 습해서; collocations: 여름 날씨가 습하다, 방이 습하다; antonym 건조하다.
Meteorological illumination noun (해 + 빛 = sunlight / sunshine); collocations: 햇빛이 강하다 / 따뜻하다, 햇빛을 쬐다 (soak in the sun), 햇빛을 받다; synonym 햇살.
Meteorological intransitive verb (to clear up); subject takes -이/가 (날씨가 개다 = weather clears up, 비가 개다); stem 개- -> 개요 / 개어서.
Meteorological noun (氣溫 = atmospheric temperature); collocations: 기온이 오르다 / 떨어지다 (temperature rises / drops), 최고 기온, 최저 기온, 영하의 기온.
Meteorological precipitation verb (to fall / come down); subject takes -이/가 (비가 내리다 = rain falls, 눈이 내리다 = snow falls); stem 내리- -> 내려요 / 내려서.
Meteorological precipitation VP ('it is raining'); synonym of 비가 내리다. Collocates with 우산을 쓰다.
Meteorological precipitation VP ('it is snowing'); synonym of 눈이 내리다. Collocates with 겨울 and 눈사람.
Meteorological storm noun (颱風 = typhoon / tropical cyclone); collocations: 태풍이 상륙하다 / 오다 (typhoon lands/arrives), 태풍 경보 (typhoon warning), 태풍 피해.
Meteorological thermal noun (零上 = temperature above zero Celsius); followed by temperature numeral + 도: 영상 15도 (15°C above zero); antonym 영하 (零下).
Meteorological thermal noun (零下 = sub-zero temperature Celsius); followed by temperature numeral + 도: 영하 10도 (minus 10°C); collocations: 기온이 영하로 떨어지다.
Meteorological wind VP ('the wind is blowing'); stem verb 불다 is ㄹ-irregular (바람이 불어요, 바람이 붑니다).
Methodology noun (方法 = method / way / manner); collocates with 좋은 방법, 해결 방법; takes modifier -(으)ㄴ/는 방법 (공부하는 방법).
Metric distance unit; pairs with Sino-Korean numerals for precise distances (100미터, 500미터). Navigational directions: 100미터쯤 가서.
Mind / heart / feelings noun; collocates with 마음에 들다 (to like / appeal to), 마음이 따뜻하다, 마음을 먹다 (make up one's mind), 마음이 편하다.
Minute counter: strictly takes Sino-Korean numbers (일 분, 십 분), not Pure Korean numbers

Mistaken assumption / expectation construction (-(으)ㄹ 줄 알았다 = 'I thought that / I assumed that [contrary to reality]'); vowel/ㄹ takes -ㄹ 줄 알았다, consonant takes -을 줄 알았다; negative is -(으)ㄹ 줄 몰랐다 ('I had no idea that...').
Modern architecture loanword noun ('commercial/high-rise building'); collocates with 높다 (빌딩이 높다), 짓다.
Moral/disposition adjective ('good-natured / kind / obedient'); applies to children, people, pets, or prices (착한 가격 = fair price); antonym is 못되다 / 나쁘다.
Motion verb ('to run / jump / race / skip'); takes locative -에서 (운동장에서 뛰다); collocates with 가슴이 뛰다 (heart beats fast), 물가가 뛰다 (prices jump).
Motorcycle loanword; vehicle counter is 대. Collocates with 타다 (오토바이를 타다).
Music noun (노래 = song / singing); collocations: 노래를 부르다 / 하다 (sing a song), 노래를 듣다 (listen to a song), 노래방 (karaoke room), 좋아하는 노래 (favorite song).
Musical genre loanword noun (rock music); collocations: 록 밴드 (rock band), 록 음악을 듣다, 록 페스티벌.
Musical instrument loanword noun (drum / drum set); paired with verb 치다 (드럼을 치다 = play drums); 드러머 (drummer).
Musical instrument loanword noun (piano); counter 대; strongly paired with verb 치다 (피아노를 치다 = play piano); 피아노 학원.
Musical instrument performance verb: paired with keyboard, string, or percussion instruments taking accusative -을/를 (피아노/기타/드럼을 치다); conjugates 쳐요 / 쳐서 / 칩니다.
Native Korean frequency adverb (always / constantly / all the time); synonym 항상 / 언제나; premodifies predicates (늘 감사해요, 늘 바쁘다).
Native Korean measurement noun (weighing scale / balance); collocates with 저울에 달다 / 재다 (weigh) and 저울에 올려놓다 (place on scale).

Native Korean ordinal numeral (셋째 = third / thirdly); (1) sequence noun/adverb: 셋째로 (thirdly / in the third place); (2) sibling order: 셋째 딸 (third daughter), 셋째 아이 (third child); sequence: 첫째 (1st), 둘째 (2nd), 셋째 (3rd), 넷째 (4th).
Native Korean temporal duration noun ('five days / 5th day'); collocates with 닷새 동안, 닷새 만에.
Native Korean temporal duration noun ('four days / 4th day'); contrast with 사흘 (3 days); takes duration particle (나흘 동안, 나흘 만에).
Native Korean temporal duration noun ('one day'); collocates with 하루 종일 (all day long), 하루 만에, 하루 빨리 (as soon as possible).
Native Korean temporal duration noun ('ten days / 10th day of the month'); collocates with 열흘 동안, 열흘 만에.
Native Korean temporal duration noun ('three days / 3rd day'); frequently confused with four but strictly means 3 days; collocates with 사흘 동안, 사흘 만에.
Native Korean temporal duration noun ('two days / 2nd day of month'); collocates with 이틀 동안, 이틀 전에, 이틀 후.
Native temporal noun (날 = day / date / weather day); collocations: 비 오는 날 (rainy day), 특별한 날 (special day), 생일날 (birthday), 그날 (that day), 어느 날 (one day); locative -에 (쉬는 날에 = on a rest day).

Native temporal noun and adverb (처음 = the beginning / the first time / initially); (1) nominal: 처음이다 (it's the first time), 처음부터 (from the beginning), 처음에 (at first); (2) adverbial use modifying predicates directly: 처음 만났을 때 (when we first met), 처음 뵙겠습니다 (pleased to meet you for the first time); antonym 마지막 / 끝.
Nature noun ('forest / woods / grove'); final consonant ㅍ assimilates before consonants; locative 숲에서 산책하다.
Necessity adjective (必要하다 = to be needed / necessary); takes needed item with nominative -이/가 (돈이/도움이 필요하다); negative is 필요 없다.
Necktie loanword; strictly collocates with specific fastening verb 매다 (넥타이를 매다 = wear a tie) and 풀다 (untie).
Negative polarity item adverb ('not particularly / not really'); obligatorily requires negative predicate (별로 안 좋다, 별로 없다, 별로 좋아하지 않다).
Negative polarity restriction particle ('nothing but / only / except'); strictly requires subsequent negative predicate (없다, 안, 못): 1000원밖에 없어요, 너밖에 몰라요; contrast with affirmative delimiter 만.
Neutral objective temporal adverb ('already / beforehand'); indicates past completion without emotional expectation (이미 끝났다, 이미 알고 있다); contrast with 벌써 (emotional surprise).
Newspaper firm workplace (新聞社); associated with journalists (기자) and takes -에 다니다.
Nominal connective/comitative particle: connects nouns (사과하고 배) or marks accompaniment (친구하고 같이). Invariant for consonant/vowel stems.
Obligation/necessity construction: stem + -아/어야 하다 (formal/written) or -아/어야 되다 (colloquial); indicates duty or requirement.
Occupation noun (公務員 = public civil servant); collocates with 되다 (공무원이 되다) and 시험 (공무원 시험).
Office technology loanword noun (fax / facsimile machine); collocations: 팩스로 보내다 (send by fax), 팩스를 받다, 팩스 번호 (fax number).
Official calendar noun (公休日 = official public holiday); collocations: 법정 공휴일 (legal holiday), 대체 공휴일 (substitute holiday); locative -에 쉬다 (공휴일에 쉬다).
Olfactory sensory noun (smell / scent / odor); collocations: 냄새가 나다 (smell comes out), 냄새를 맡다 (smell/sniff), 맛있는 냄새 (delicious aroma), 냄새를 피우다.
Opposite side spatial noun (across the street); synonym of 맞은편. Takes locative -에 (길 건너편에 있다).
Oppositional noun (反對 = opposite / contrary / objection); collocates with 반대 방향 (opposite direction), 반대쪽; 반대하다 (to oppose / object to).

Optative wishing expression ('I wish / I hope that...'); combines conditional -(으)면 with past-form adjective 좋겠다; consonant stem takes -으면 좋겠다 (비가 그치면 좋겠어요, 찾으면 좋겠어요); vowel or ㄹ stem takes -면 좋겠다 (가면 좋겠어요, 살면 좋겠어요); emphatic variant -았/었으면 좋겠다 (비가 그쳤으면 좋겠어요 = strong wish for unrealized/counterfactual state).
Oral mastication verb ('to chew / masticate'); takes food with -을/를 (음식을 꼭꼭 씹어 먹다, 껌을 씹다); slang: ignore message (메시지를 씹다).
Organization verb (整理 + 하다 = to arrange / organize / tidy up); takes object with -을/를 (방을 정리하다, 책상을 정리하다, 생각을 정리하다).
Outerwear loanword noun ('jumper / jacket / windbreaker'); selectional restriction: takes wearable verb 입다 (점퍼를 입다/벗다); counter: 벌.
Outerwear loanword; counter is 벌. Collocates with 입다 (코트를 입다) and winter/cold weather.
Outward motion verb ('to go out'); takes exit path with -로 (3번 출구로 나가다) and room origin with -에서.
Overcast/cloudy sky adjective (날씨/하늘이 흐리다); antonym of 맑다. Also applies to murky water or blurry vision.
Page counter: pairs with Sino-Korean numbers (일 쪽, 십 쪽)
Pairs with transitive verb 보다 (영화를 보다)
Pairs with transitive verb 하다 (숙제를 하다)
Pairs with 듣다 (수업을 듣다 - take a class) or 하다 (수업을 하다)
Pairs with 하다 (대화하다) or 나누다 (대화를 나누다)
Pants/trousers; counter is 벌. Collocates with lower-body/general apparel verb 입다 (바지를 입다).
Paper toiletry noun (休紙 = toilet paper / tissue / waste paper); counter: 개, 롤; traditional housewarming gift symbolizing matters unraveling smoothly.
Passive accumulation/congestion verb ('to be pushed / backlogged / traffic delayed'); takes subject with -이/가 (차가 밀리다 = cars backed up, 일이 밀리다 = work backlogged).
Passive delivery verb (配達되다 = to be delivered); subject takes -이/가 (음식이 배달되다, 택배가 배달되었어요); active counterpart is 배달하다.
Passive/blockage verb ('to be blocked / clogged / jammed'); takes subject with -이/가 (길이 막히다 = traffic is jammed, 코가 막히다 = stuffy nose, 말이 막히다).
Passive/inchoative opening verb ('to open / be held'); paired passive of 열다; takes subject with -이/가 (문이 열리다, 마음이 열리다, 축제가 열리다).
Passive/intransitive visual verb ('to be seen / visible'); takes visible subject with -이/가 (오른쪽에 병원이 보일 거예요).
Passport noun (旅券); essential travel document. Collocates with 챙기다 (pack), 보여주다 (present), 만들다.
Paternal aunt kinship noun (姑母 = father's sister); husband is 고모부 (姑母夫); contrast with 이모 (maternal aunt).
Paternal grandfather; requires subject honorifics (할아버지께서).
Paternal grandmother; requires subject honorifics (할머니께서 진지를 드시다).
Pedestrian crosswalk noun (橫斷步道); strictly collocates with traversal verb 건너다 (횡단보도를 건너다).
Pedestrian footbridge overpass (陸橋); collocates with 건너다 (cross) and 올라가다/내려가다.
Perception adjective ('bright / light / sharp'); collocates with 빛/방이 밝다, 성격이 밝다 (cheerful), 눈/귀가 밝다 (sharp vision/hearing); antonym is 어둡다.
Perception adjective ('dark / dim'); ㅂ-irregular: 어두워요 / 어두워서; collocates with 방이 어둡다, 안색이 어둡다 (somber face), 귀/눈이 어둡다 (poor hearing/vision); antonym is 밝다.
Performing arts noun (演劇 = theatrical play / stage performance); counter 편; collocations: 연극을 보다 / 관람하다, 연극 배우 (stage actor), 연극 티켓.
Performing arts verb (演技하다 = act / perform); argument frame: [Noun:art]에서 연기하다 (드라마/영화/연극에서 연기하다); conjugates 연기해요 / 연기해서.
Perfume noun (香水); bottle counter is 병. Strictly takes spray/application verb 뿌리다 (향수를 뿌리다). Homonym with 鄕愁 (homesickness).
Permission auxiliary construction: verb stem + -아/어도 되다 ('may / it is okay to / allowed to'); e.g. 들어가도 돼요, 먹어도 돼요; negative counterpart is -으면 안 되다.
Permission construction: stem + -아/어도 되다 ('it is permissible to / may I'); antonym is -(으)면 안 되다 (prohibition).
Personality/character noun (性格); collocates with 좋다/나쁘다, 급하다 (impatient), 느긋하다, 활발하다, 조용하다.
Pharmaceutical compound noun (기침 + 藥 = cough medicine / cough syrup); paired with verb 먹다 (기침약을 먹다 = take cough medicine).
Pharmaceutical compound noun (便秘藥 = laxative / constipation medication); paired with verb 먹다 / 복용하다 (변비약을 먹다).
Pharmaceutical compound noun (感氣藥 = cold medicine); collocations: 감기약을 짓다 / 사다 / 먹다 (take cold medicine); contrast with 두통약 (painkiller).
Pharmaceutical compound noun (消毒藥 = antiseptic / disinfectant); collocations: 상처에 소독약을 바르다 (apply antiseptic to a wound).
Pharmaceutical compound noun (頭痛藥 = headache medicine / pain reliever / analgesic); paired with verb 먹다 (두통약을 먹다); synonym 진통제.
Pharmaceutical noun (消化劑 = digestive medicine / aid); paired with verb 먹다 (체했을 때 소화제를 먹다 = take digestive medicine for indigestion).
Pharmacy facility noun (藥局); takes locative -에서 with 약을 사다.
Phone number noun; digits are read using Sino-Korean numerals, with hyphens pronounced as 에. Collocates with 가르쳐 주다 / 물어보다.
Phone status predicate (通話中 + -이다); indicates the line is busy or user is currently engaged in a call.
Physical appearance adjective ('slender / slim'); modifies person body/figure; antonym is 뚱뚱하다.
Physical burden/baggage noun ('luggage / load / baggage'); collocates with 짐을 싸다 (pack), 짐을 풀다 (unpack), 짐을 들다/맡기다.
Physical item / merchandise noun (物件); general counter is 개. Collocates with 사다, 팔다, 찾다.
Physical perception verb ('to touch / handle / feel with hands'); takes object with -을/를 (작품을 만지지 마세요, 만져 보다).
Physical traction verb ('to pull / draw toward / attract'); takes object with -을/를 (문을 당기다 = pull door); appetite idiom (입맛이 당기다); antonym is 밀다 (push).
Physiological action verb ('to doze / nod off / nap lightly'); ㄹ-irregular stem: 졸아요 / 조니 / 좁니다; locative -에서 (수업 시간에 졸다, 지하철에서 졸다).
Physiological noun (blood); collocations: 피가 나다 (bleed / blood comes out), 피를 흘리다 (bleed profusely), 피를 뽑다 (draw blood for a test), 혈액형 (blood type).
Physiological noun (sweat / perspiration); strongly collocates with 땀이 나다 (sweat occurs), 땀을 흘리다 (break a sweat), 땀을 닦다 (wipe sweat).
Physiological noun (消化 = digestion); collocations: 소화가 잘되다 / 안되다 (good/poor digestion), 소화제 (digestive aid medicine), 소화가 되다.
Physiological state adjective (to be sleepy / drowsy); stem 졸리- -> 졸려요 / 졸려서 / 졸리면; collocations: 너무 졸리다, 운전할 때 졸리면 쉬어가세요.
Physiological state idiom (목이 + 마르다 = throat dries / thirsty); 르-irregular: 목이 말라요 / 말라서; antonym is 배가 부르다/갈증 해소.
Physiological symptom verb phrase (body trembles / shivers); caused by cold, fever, or nervousness: 추워서 몸이 떨려요; passive stem 떨리- -> 떨려요 / 떨려서.
Placement verb ('to put / lay down / place'); takes object with -을/를 and location with -에 (책상 위에 책을 놓다); auxiliary -아/어 놓다 indicates resultant state preservation.
Placement verb ('to put / place / leave behind'); takes object with -을/를 and location with -에 (가방을 방에 두다); auxiliary -아/어 두다 indicates keeping in a certain state for future.
Placement verb ('to put down / lay / set down / let go'); takes object with -을/를 and location with -에 (책상에 놓다, 손을 놓다); auxiliary -아/어 놓다 indicates preserving resultant state.
Plain form; honorific counterpart is 생신 for elders/seniors. Collocates with 축하하다 (생일 축하합니다).
Plain intransitive verb; honorific counterpart is 주무시다 for elders/seniors. Collocates with sleep nouns (잠을 자다).

Plain non-polite declarative sentence ending (해라체); used in writing, internal thought, or speaking to close equals/juniors; action verbs take -ㄴ다 (vowel) or -는다 (consonant) (간다, 먹는다); descriptive verbs take -다 (예쁘다, 좋다).
Plain non-polite imperative ending (해라체 command); vowel/positive takes -아라, negative/other takes -어라, 하다 becomes 해라 (먹어라, 가라, 공부해라); used toward children, animals, or in exclamation (어라 = oops!).
Plain non-polite propositive ending (해라체 proposal: 'let's do X'); attaches directly to action verb stems (가자, 밥 먹자, 쉬자); used between close equals and to younger people.
Pleasantly warm adjective; applies to ambient weather (날씨), beverages/food, and human warmth (마음이 따뜻하다).
Pluralizing suffix; primarily attaches to animate/person nouns (사람들, 아이들). Optional in Korean when quantity is clear from context.
Pocket/pouch noun ('pocket / small pouch'); collocates with 주머니에 넣다/손을 넣다; 주머니 사정 (financial situation).
Polite 2nd person plural addressing pronoun/noun (여러 + 分 = everyone / ladies and gentlemen); used in public addresses, speeches, classrooms (여러분 안녕하세요).
Polite conversational formula requesting brief pause/wait ('Just a moment, please'); common on phone calls and service counters.
Polite conversational opener ('Excuse me, but...'); conventional formula before asking strangers for directions or information.
Polite honorific kinship noun (夫人 = another person's wife / Madam); used respectfully when referring to someone else's wife (선생님 부인); self-reference uses 아내 or 집사람.
Polite interrogative future intention ending ('are you going to / will you...?'); contraction of -(으)ㄹ 것인가요; vowel/ㄹ takes -ㄹ 건가요? (갈 건가요?), consonant takes -을 건가요? (먹을 건가요?).
Polite request/imperative ending: vowel stem takes -세요, consonant stem takes -으세요. Also serves as subject honorific informal non-past.
Polysemous adverbial phrase (앞 + -으로): (1) temporal from now on / in the future (앞으로 열심히 하겠습니다, 앞으로도); (2) spatial toward the front (앞으로 나오세요).
Polysemous light verb taking accusative -을/를: (1) pay money (돈/등록금/공과금을 내다), (2) hand in/submit (서류/신청서/숙제를 내다), (3) produce/bring forth (시간을 내다, 소리를 내다, 화를 내다).
Polysemous native noun: (1) nocturnal time (night; locative 밤에; antonym 낮 = daytime; collocations: 늦은 밤, 밤새도록); (2) edible tree fruit (chestnut; 군밤 = roasted chestnut).
Polysemous noun: (1) car/vehicle (차를 타다/운전하다; counter 대), (2) tea/beverage (차를 마시다; counter 잔).
Polysemous noun: (1) City hall facility (市廳, e.g. 서울시청); (2) TV watching/viewing (視聽, e.g. 시청자, 시청률); takes locative -에서 or allative -에.
Polysemous noun: (1) fruit persimmon (counter: 개; 곶감 = dried persimmon); (2) intuition/feeling (感, 감이 좋다/오다 = have a hunch).
Polysemous noun: (1) furniture bookcase (冊欌 = bookshelf/bookcase; 책장에 책을 꽂다); (2) page of book (冊張, 책장을 넘기다).
Polysemous noun: (1) line / queue of people (줄을 서다 = queue up); (2) string / cord / rope (줄을 묶다); (3) guitar/instrument string.
Polysemous noun: (1) musical instrument loanword (guitar; paired with verb 치다: 기타를 치다 = play guitar); (2) Sino-Korean 'and others / etc.' (其他; 기타 사항, 기타 등등).
Polysemous noun: (1) noodles (麵, e.g. 라면, 냉면, 면을 삶다); (2) side/facet/surface (面, e.g. 긍정적인 면).
Polysemous noun: (1) personal seal / stamp (圖章 = inkan/stamp used for legal/banking contracts); paired with 도장을 찍다 (stamp/affix a seal); (2) martial arts dojo / training hall (道場).
Polysemous noun: (1) physiological fever/heat (熱; 열이 나다 = run a fever, 열을 재다 = measure temperature); (2) pure Korean cardinal number 10 (열); (3) line/column (列).
Polysemous noun: (1) salty taste / seasoning of dish (간이 맞다 = well-seasoned, 간을 보다 = taste/check seasoning, 간을 하다 = season); (2) organ liver (肝).
Polysemous noun: (1) speech / words / spoken language (말을 하다, 한국말, 거짓말); honorific suppletive 말씀; (2) animal horse (counter: 마리); (3) end (연말, 월말).
Polysemous noun: (1) street / avenue / thoroughfare (거리에서 만나다, 대학로 거리); (2) distance / span (거리 = 距離, 거리가 멀다/가깝다).
Polysemous noun: (1) temporal former times / before (以前 = previous time / prior to; e.g. 10시 이전, 졸업 이전); (2) physical relocation (移轉 = moving office/premises).
Polysemous noun/counter: (1) direction / side (이쪽, 저쪽, 오른쪽, 반대쪽); (2) counter for pages (쪽 = 1 page, 50쪽); (3) counter for fruit slices/cloves (마늘 한 쪽).
Polysemous noun/counter: (1) second of time (秒 = second; takes Sino-Korean numerals: 10초, 30초); (2) beginning of a period (初 = beginning: 월초, 학기 초); (3) candle (초를 켜다 = light a candle).
Polysemous perception verb: (1) look/watch (영화를 보다, 책을 보다); (2) take an exam (시험을 보다); (3) check/taste (맛을 보다, 장을 보다 = grocery shop); auxiliary -아/어 보다 (try doing).
Polysemous predicate: (1) correct/right (정답이 맞다); (2) fit size/clothing (사이즈가 맞다); (3) agree/match (성격이 맞다); (4) action verb get hit / rained on (비를 맞다, 주사를 맞다).
Polysemous profession noun: (1) driver/technician (技士 = engineer/technician/driver; addressed politely as 기사님, e.g. 택시 기사님); (2) news article (記事, 신문 기사); (3) knight (騎士).

Polysemous pronoun/determiner/filler: (1) humble 1st person singular 'I/me' (저 + 가 -> 제가); (2) distal determiner 'that over there' (저 사람); (3) polite conversational hesitation filler 'um / excuse me' (저, 실례지만).
Polysemous Sino-Korean noun: (1) inclusive comparative bound noun (以上 = [Number] or more / above / beyond; e.g. 18세 이상, 2시간 이상; antonym 이하); (2) abnormality (異常 = malfunction / strangeness; 이상이 생기다).
Polysemous spatial and physiological noun: (1) spatial interior (inside / depth; 가방 속에, 물속에; antonym 겉); (2) stomach / inner mind (속이 쓰리다 = heartburn, 속이 시원하다 = relieved).

Polysemous transitive s-irregular verb: (1) cook rice (밥을 짓다), (2) construct building (집을 짓다), (3) prepare medicine (약을 짓다), (4) make a facial expression (미소를 짓다), (5) name/compose (이름/노래를 짓다); s-irregular (지어요 / 지어서 / 지으면).
Polysemous transitive verb: (1) search/look for (물건을 찾다), (2) find/discover (답을 찾다), (3) withdraw/retrieve funds or items (돈을 찾다 = withdraw money from bank/ATM, 짐을 찾다).
Polysemous transitive verb: (1) to search/find (물건을 찾다), (2) to withdraw money (돈을 찾다), (3) to visit (친구를 찾아가다).
Polysemous verb of living/spending time; greeting formula: 어떻게 지내세요? / 잘 지내요 (How are you doing? / Doing well).
Polysemous verb: (1) action verb to count numbers (수를 세다, 돈을 세다); (2) descriptive verb strong / fierce (힘이 세다, 바람이 세다).
Polysemous verb: (1) dip food into sauce (소스에 찍다); (2) take a photograph (사진을 찍다); (3) stamp/seal (도장을 찍다); (4) shoot a video/movie.
Polysemous verb: (1) intransitive wake up (잠에서 깨다, 술이 깨다); (2) transitive break/smash brittle object (유리를 깨다, 그릇을 깨다).
Polysemous verb: (1) roll up (김밥을 말다); (2) mix rice into broth (국에 밥을 말아 먹다); (3) negative auxiliary in -지 말다 ('refrain from / do not'); ㄹ-irregular stem.
Polysemous verb: (1) send object/mail with dative -에게/한테, (2) spend time (주말을 잘 보내세요).
Polysemous verb: (1) steam food (만두를 찌다, 옥수수를 찌다); (2) gain weight (살이 찌다); (3) sweltering hot weather (날씨가 찌다).
Polysemous verb: (1) time duration (한 시간 걸리다), (2) illness with dative (감기에 걸리다), (3) hanging on wall.
Polysemous verb: (1) to hang something on wall (벽에 그림을 걸다); (2) to make a phone call (전화를 걸다); (3) to initiate talk/fight (말을 걸다, 싸움을 걸다); ㄹ-irregular stem.
Polysemous verb: (1) to occur / arise (일이/문제가 생기다, 돈이 생기다); (2) appearance (잘생기다 = handsome, 못생기다 = ugly, 어떻게 생겼어요?).
Polysemous verb: (1) to pack/wrap (짐을 싸다 = pack luggage, 도시락을 싸다 = pack lunchbox, 선물 포장); (2) homophone cheap (값이 싸다).
Polysemous verb: (1) to peel/pare fruit (사과를 깎다); (2) to discount price (값을 깎아 주다); (3) to trim hair/nails (머리/손톱을 깎다).
Polysemous verb: (1) to use/spend money, tools, language (돈을 쓰다, 컴퓨터를 쓰다, 한국말을 쓰다); (2) write (글을 쓰다); (3) wear on head/face (모자/안경을 쓰다); (4) taste bitter (약이 쓰다).
Polysemous: (1) identifier number suffix with Sino-Korean numerals (1번 버스 = Bus #1); (2) frequency counter with Pure Korean numerals (한 번 = once).
Polysemous: (1) pre-nominal determiner/관형사 'new' modifying following noun directly (새 옷, 새 신발, 새 차); (2) noun bird (counter: 마리).
Postal delivery noun (小包 = parcel / package); paired with verbs 보내다 / 부치다 (send a package) and 받다 (receive a package); counter 개.
Postal sending verb taking accusative -을/를 (편지/소포/짐을 부치다 = mail a letter/package); conjugates 부쳐요 / 부쳐서 / 부칩니다.
Postal service proper/compound noun (國際特急 = international express mail / EMS); collocates with 국제 특급으로 보내다 (send via international express / EMS).
Postal stationery noun (葉書 = postcard); counter 장; collocations: 엽서를 쓰다 / 부치다 / 보내다, 그림엽서 (picture postcard).
Postal stationery noun (郵票 = postage stamp); counter 장 (sheet/stamp); strongly collocates with verb 붙이다 (우표를 붙이다 = stick a stamp).
Postal/transport compound noun (배便 = sea mail / surface shipping / ship route); instrumental 배편으로 (by boat/sea mail; 배편으로 보내다); contrast with 항공편 (airmail).
Postural and halt verb ('to stand up / come to a halt / queue'); inflects 서요 / 서서; collocates with 줄을 서다 (stand in line), 차가 서다 (car stops).

Potentiality and know-how construction (-(으)ㄹ 줄 알다 / 모르다 = 'know / not know how to do X'); attaches to Action verbs: vowel/ㄹ takes -ㄹ 줄 알다 (운전할 줄 알아요), consonant takes -을 줄 알다 (만들 줄 알아요); contrast with cognitive conjecture.
Potentiality/ability construction: verb stem + -(으)ㄹ 수 있다. Expresses ability or situational possibility; antonym is -(으)ㄹ 수 없다.
Pragmatic trial adverb ('give it a try / once'); distinct from spaced numeral counter 한 번 (literally 1 time). Modifies experiential clauses.
Pre-nominal adnominal determiner/관형사 ('first'); modifies following noun directly without particle (첫 월급, 첫 만남, 첫사랑, 첫날).
Pre-nominal question determiner: must precede a category Noun (e.g. 무슨 음식, 무슨 영화)
Prehension verb ('to catch / grab / grasp / hold'); takes object with -을/를 (손을 잡다, 택시를 잡다, 범인을 잡다, 기회를 잡다).
Prerequisite conditional connective (-아/어야 = 'only if / only when / must do X for Y'); attaches to verb/adjective stems via -아/어 (노력해야 성공한다, 비자가 있어야 갈 수 있다).
Present adnominal modifier suffix on action verbs (공부하는 학생); stem final ㄹ drops before -는 (살다 -> 사는).
Present time adverbial: pairs with present or ongoing tense
Price adjective; antonym of 비싸다. Homonym with action verb 싸다 (to pack/wrap: 짐을 싸다).
Price adjective; antonym of 싸다. Takes commodity or price as subject (값이 비싸다, 옷이 비싸다).
Primary educational institution noun (初等學校 = elementary / primary school; 6-year curriculum); collocations: 초등학교에 입학하다, 초등학생 (elementary student).
Print media loanword noun ('poster'); counter: 장; collocates with 포스터를 붙이다 (put up a poster).
Private B&B lodging facility (民泊 + 집); collocates with 묵다 or 민박하다.
Proactive temporal adverb (in advance / beforehand / ahead of time); premodifies preparation predicates (미리 예약하다, 미리 말하다, 미리 준비하다); synonym 사전에.
Profession/status noun (演藝人 = celebrity / entertainer / star); counter 명 / 분; collocates with 연예인이 되다, 유명 연예인.
Progressive aspect construction: verb stem + -는 중이다 ('in the middle of doing'); attaches to action verbs (식사하는 중이다, 통화 중이다).
Prohibition auxiliary construction: verb stem + -(으)면 안 되다 ('must not / should not / prohibited'); consonant stem takes -으면, vowel/ㄹ takes -면 (여기서 담배를 피우면 안 돼요, 떠들면 안 돼요).
Prohibition construction: stem + -(으)면 안 되다 ('must not / it is not allowed'); negative counterpart of -아/어도 되다.

Prohibitive alternative connective clause (-지 말고 = 'instead of doing X / do not do X and rather do Y'); attaches directly to Action verb stems (집에 있지 말고 나가요, 걱정하지 말고 쉬세요); followed by alternative suggestion or command.
Pronounced [가치] via palatalization (구개음화). Collocates with comitative particles: -와/과 같이, -(이)랑 같이, -하고 같이.
Pronounced [마니] (ㅎ silent before vowel). Quantity adverb modifying verbs (많이 먹다) or adjectives.
Pronounced [장년] via nasalization (비음화). Takes time particle -에 (작년에). Requires past tense.
Proper geographic abbreviation (弘大 = Hongik University area / bustling youth arts & nightlife district); locative -에서.
Proper geographic noun (仁寺洞 = traditional cultural district in Seoul); locative -에서 (인사동에서 전통 찻집에 가다).
Proper geographic noun (南海 = Southern Sea of Korea / South Sea county); locative -에서.
Proper geographic noun (漢拏山 = Hallasan mountain on Jeju Island, highest peak in South Korea); collocates with 등산하다, 올라가다.
Proper noun acronym (TOPIK = Test of Proficiency in Korean / 한국어능력시험); collocations: 토픽 시험을 치다 / 보다, 토픽 몇 급이에요?, 토픽 점수.
Proper noun river park in Seoul; takes locative -에서 with outdoor activities (한강공원에서 자전거를 타다).
Proper noun: Korean historic cultural city (全州); famous for 전주 한옥마을 and 전주 비빔밥.
Propositive sentence ending in 하게-style (하소서/하게체 proposal: 'let us / let's'); used by older persons to adult younger equals/subordinates (이제 시작하세, 같이 가세).
Propositive/deliberative interrogative ending ('shall we? / shall I?'); 1st person plural/singular subject asking listener's intention (같이 커피 마실까요?, 제가 도와드릴까요?).

Prospective intention/assumption reason connective clause (-을/ㄹ 테니까 = 'because I will / since it will be / assuming that'); 1st person subject expresses speaker's strong intent or promise (내가 갈 테니까 기다려요), 2nd/3rd person expresses speaker's strong supposition/assumption (비가 올 테니까 우산을 챙기세요); followed by suggestion, request, or command.
Prototypical bound noun (의존명사); must be preceded by adnominal modifier (-(으)ㄴ, -는, -(으)ㄹ 것). Contracts to 거/게/건/걸.
Proximal demonstrative adjective ('to be like this'); ㅎ-irregular: 이래요 / 이런 (adnominal 'such a / this kind of'); adverbial is 이렇게 ('like this / so').

Proximal demonstrative determiner (이 = this); prenominal modifier preceding noun: 이 사람 (this person), 이 책 (this book), 이 곳 (this place); refers to entities physically or psychologically close to speaker.
Proximal directional noun ('this way / our side'); navigational formula: 이쪽으로 오세요.
Psychological and behavioral noun (習慣 = personal habit / custom); collocations: 좋은/나쁜 습관, 습관을 기르다 (cultivate habit), 식습관 (dietary habit), 생활 습관.
Psychological anticipation noun (期待 = expectation / anticipation); collocates with 기대를 하다/모으다, 기대에 부응하다.
Psychological loanword noun ('stress'); collocates with 받다 (스트레스를 받다 = get stressed), 풀다 (스트레스를 풀다 = relieve stress), 쌓이다 (stress accumulates).
Psychological state adjective ('to have nothing to do / feel unoccupied'); contrasts with 지루하다 (bored by external stimuli).
Psychological state adjective (不安하다 = anxious / uneasy / insecure); collocates with 마음이 불안하다.

Psychological state noun (氣分 = mood / feeling / atmosphere); collocations: 기분이 좋다 (to feel good / be in a good mood), 기분이 나쁘다 (to feel bad / be in a bad mood), 기분을 풀다 (relieve bad feelings), 기분 전환 (change of pace / refreshing oneself).
Public announcement/presentation verb (發表 + 하다 = to present / announce / publish); takes topic with -을/를 (결과를 발표하다, 앞에서 발표하다).
Public outdoor space; takes locative -에서 for walking/relaxing (공원에서 산책하다).
Public taxi vehicle; vehicle counter is 대. Collocates with 타다 (ride), 잡다 (hail), 내리다 (get off), and instrumental -로 (by taxi).
Public transit facility compound (老弱者席 = priority seats for elderly, pregnant, injured, disabled); collocates with 노약자석에 앉다/양보하다.
Public transportation noun; takes 타다 (지하철을 타다) and instrumental -로 (지하철로 가다). Station noun is 지하철역.
Publishing compound noun (漫畵 + 冊 = comic book / graphic novel); counter 권 (volume); collocations: 만화책을 빌리다 / 읽다, 만화방 (comic book parlor).
Pure Korean cardinal 20; mutates to attributive form 스무 before measure words (스무 살, 스무 개).
Pure Korean cardinal numeral (30); attributive adnominal form is 서른 (서른 살); Sino-Korean equivalent is 삼십 (30).
Pure Korean cardinal numeral (40); attributive adnominal form is 마흔 (마흔 살, 마흔 명); Sino-Korean equivalent is 사십 (40).
Pure Korean cardinal numeral (50); attributive adnominal form is 쉰 (쉰 살); Sino-Korean equivalent is 오십 (50).
Pure Korean cardinal numeral (60); attributive adnominal form is 예순 (예순 살); Sino-Korean equivalent is 육십 (60).
Pure Korean cardinal numeral (70); attributive adnominal form is 일흔 (일흔 살); Sino-Korean equivalent is 칠십 (70).
Pure Korean cardinal numeral (80); attributive adnominal form is 여든 (여든 살); Sino-Korean equivalent is 팔십 (80).
Pure Korean cardinal numeral (90); attributive adnominal form is 아흔 (아흔 살); Sino-Korean equivalent is 구십 (90).
Pure Korean daily frequency adverb (날 + delimiter -마다); native Korean equivalent of Sino-Korean 매일.
Pure Korean general place noun; head noun for adnominal modification (좋은 곳, 따뜻한 곳, 이곳).
Pure Korean noun: (1) duration of months (한 달, 두 달); (2) celestial moon. Duration uses Pure Korean numerals.
Pure Korean price noun; double batchim ㅄ [갑/갑씨]. Subject of 비싸다/싸다/오르다/내리다.
Pure Korean term for 'this year'; can take -에 (올해에) or stand alone adverbially.
Purpose-motion construction: verb stem + -(으)러 paired strictly with directional motion verbs (가다, 오다, 다니다).

Quantity emphasis particle ('as many/much as / no less than'); expresses surprise at large number/amount; consonant takes 이나 (10병이나), vowel takes 나 (5개나); duplicate curriculum entry corresponding to ID 1334.
Quantity emphasis particle ('as much as / as many as / no less than'); expresses surprise at large quantity/duration; consonant takes 이나 (3시간이나, 10병이나), vowel takes 나 (사과를 5개나).
Quantity/degree adverb ('a little/slightly'); contracts colloquially to 좀. Modifies verbs, adjectives, or nouns.
Question numeral: must precede a counter noun (e.g. 몇 시, 몇 명, 몇 개)
Racket sport; collocates strictly with 치다 (탁구를 치다), not 하다. Venue takes 탁구장.
Racket sport; collocates strictly with 치다 (테니스를 치다). Venue takes 테니스장.
Rain footwear noun (長靴 = tall rubber rain boots); counter 켤레; paired with footwear wearable verb 신다 (비 오는 날에 장화를 신다 = wear rain boots).
Rain gear; collocates with weather 비가 오다 and action verbs 쓰다 (우산을 쓰다 = use/hold umbrella), 펴다 (open), 접다 (fold).
Rainwear apparel noun (비 + 옷 = raincoat); counter 벌; paired with wearable verb 입다 (비옷을 입다 = wear a raincoat); Sino-Korean synonym 우비 (雨衣).
Reciprocal social conflict verb (to fight / argue / quarrel); argument frame: [Person]와/과 싸우다 (친구와 말다툼하고 싸우다); stem 싸우- -> 싸워요 / 싸워서.
Reciprocal verb: takes comitative partner with -와/과, -하고, or -(이)랑 (친구와 데이트하다).
Recreational activity verb (낚시하다 = to fish / go angling); argument frame: [Place]에서 낚시하다 (바다/강에서 낚시하다); collocations: 낚시를 가다 (go fishing), 낚싯대 (fishing rod).
Recreational compound noun (camping + 場 = campsite / camping ground); locative -에 가다 / -에서 캠핑하다.
Reduction verb ('to diminish / shrink / decrease'); ㄹ-irregular: 줄어요 / 주니 / 줍니다; takes subject with -이/가 (체중이 줄다, 인구가 줄다); antonym is 늘다.
Reduction/portioning verb ('to lessen / dish out / portion'); takes object with -을/를 (음식을 접시에 덜다, 짐을 덜다, 걱정을 덜다); ㄹ-irregular stem.
Refreshingly cool autumn weather adjective (선선한 날씨/바람); synonymous with 시원하다.
Regional telephone area code noun; digits read in Sino-Korean numerals.
Regular commuting/attendance verb; takes workplace or educational institution with -에 (회사/학교에 다니다).
Regular ㄷ verb: stem final ㄷ is retained before vowels (받아요, 받으면). Takes source particle -에게서/한테서 (or -에게/한테) and accusative -을/를.
Regular ㅂ adjective: retains ㅂ before vowels (좁아요, 좁으면). Antonym is 넓다.
Relational noun (夫婦 = married couple / husband and wife); collocates with 신혼부부 (newlyweds), 부부 싸움 (marital argument); counter 쌍 (couple).
Relocation verb (移徙 + 하다 = to move house); takes origin with -에서, destination with -(으)로 / -에 (새 집으로 이사하다).
Repetitive manner adverb ('repeatedly / constantly / over and over'); expresses persistence, often unwanted (자꾸 전화가 오다, 자꾸 잊어버리다, 자꾸 눈물이 나다).
Repetitive training verb (練習 + 하다 = to practice / rehearse / drill); takes skill or language with -을/를 (발음을 연습하다, 수영을 연습하다).

Reported reason connective clause ('since they say that / because it is reported that'); Action verbs: consonant takes -는다고 하니까 (비가 온다고 하니까), vowel takes -ㄴ다고 하니까; Descriptive verbs take -다고 하니까 (춥다고 하니까); followed by suggestion/imperative.
Repulsion verb ('to push / shove / shave hair'); ㄹ-irregular: 밀어요 / 미니 / 밉니다; takes object with -을/를 (문을 밀다, 수염을 밀다); antonym is 당기다.
Reputation adjective (有名하다 = famous / well-known); takes topic/complement -로 유명하다 (관광지로 유명하다) or subject -이/가 유명하다.
Residential architecture loanword noun ('veranda / balcony / utility porch'); locative -에/-에서 (베란다에 화분을 놓다).
Residential culinary room noun ('kitchen'); final consonant ㅋ neutralizes to [ㄱ] before consonants and aspirates before vowels (부엌에 [부어케]); locative -에서 (부엌에서 요리하다).
Residential room noun (居室 = living room); locative -에서 (거실에서 TV를 보다).
Residential room noun (書齋 = study room / home library); locative -에서 (서재에서 책을 읽다).
Residential room noun (浴室 = bathroom / shower room); locative -에서 (욕실에서 씻다).
Resort lodging condominium loanword; collocates with 묵다 and 예약하다.
Respectful title concord: pairs with honorific verb/predicate markers
Restaurant portion counter: strictly takes Sino-Korean numbers (일 인분, 삼 인분)
Restaurant/store service call marker: attracts server attention. Politeness marker -요 attached to deictic pronoun 여기.
Restroom facility noun (化粧室); collocates with directional 가다 and hygiene verbs 손을 씻다.
Retail category compound (fashion + 雜貨 = miscellaneous fashion goods / accessories, e.g. bags, hats, scarves, belts); collocates with 패션잡화 코너.
Retail noun (賣場 = store / sales counter / floor); collocates with 백화점 매장, 매장을 둘러보다.
Retail store noun; takes locative -에서 with 물건을 사다/팔다.

Retrospective habitual / imperfective adnominal suffix (-던 = 'which I used to / which was ongoing'); attaches directly to verb/adjective stems without batchim distinction (자주 듣던 노래, 다니던 학교, 예쁘던 얼굴); contrast with completed -았던/었던.

Retrospective observational sentence ending (-던데요 = 'as I recall / I noticed that / it was...'); expresses speaker's firsthand recollection with mild surprise or feedback; attaches directly to stems (어제 춥던데요, 맛있던데요).
Return motion verb towards speaker ('to come back / return'); contrasts with 돌아가다 (return away from speaker). Takes goal with -에 (집에 돌아오다).
Reunion greeting formula (오랜만 + 이다 = 'It has been a long time / Long time no see'); adverbial form 오랜만에 (after a long time).
Right direction noun; antonym of 왼쪽. Takes directional particle -으로 (오른쪽으로 가세요 = go right).
Road intersection noun (三거리 = three-way junction / T-junction); collocates with 삼거리에서 좌회전하다; contrast with 사거리 (four-way intersection).
Role/transformation/identity particle ('as / into / for'); marks role or outcome (선물로 주다, 반장으로 뽑히다, 물이 얼음으로 변하다).
Roll counter is 줄 (e.g. 김밥 두 줄). Portions take Sino-Korean -인분 (e.g. 김밥 1인분).
Rote learning verb ('to memorize / commit to memory'); takes content with -을/를 (단어를 외우다, 전화번호를 외우다).
Safety boundary compound noun (安全線 = safety line); collocates with 안전선 밖으로 물러서다 (step back behind the safety line).
Sanitary protective accessory (face mask); counter 개; paired with wearable verb 쓰다 (마스크를 쓰다 = wear a face mask) and unwear verb 벗다; 미세먼지 마스크.
Scenery attribute: pairs with visual/aesthetic descriptive verbs (아름답다, 좋다, 멋있다)
Scheduling postponement verb (延期하다 = postpone / delay); takes event/schedule with -을/를 (약속을/회의를 연기하다; synonym 미루다); conjugates 연기해요 / 연기해서.
School institutional excursion (修學旅行 = school field trip / class retreat); collocations: 제주도로 수학여행을 가다 (go on school trip to Jeju Island).
School vacation verb (放學 + 하다); indicates commencement of academic break (학교가 방학하다). Antonym is 개학하다.
Schoolmate noun (同窓 = alumnus / schoolmate / classmate); collocates with 초등학교 동창, 동창회 (alumni reunion).
Season noun (季節); encompasses 봄, 여름, 가을, 겨울. Standard inquiry: 무슨 계절을 좋아해요?
Secondary educational institution noun (中學校 = middle school / junior high; 3-year curriculum); collocations: 중학교를 졸업하다, 중학생 (middle school student).
Secondary educational institution noun (高等學校 = high school; 3-year curriculum in Korea); collocations: 고등학교를 졸업하다, 고등학생 (high school student).
Sentence-initial adversative conjunction ('however / but'); connects contrasting sentences. Synonymous with 하지만.
Sentence-initial causal conjunction ('so / therefore'); links preceding reason to subsequent result.
Sentence-initial conjunctive adverb linking two clauses or sentences. Can also coordinate items in a list.
Seoul subway station proper noun (汝矣島驛 = Line 5 & 9 interchange station in financial district Yeouido).
Service price noun (料金 = fare / service rate / fee); collocates with 교통 요금, 요금을 내다/지불하다.
Service worker/employee noun (從業員); counter is 명 (plain) or 분 (polite). Works at 식당/가게.
Serving dish/bowl counter: pairs with food/soup servings (국 한 그릇, 밥 두 그릇)
Short-form pre-verbal negation: precedes verb/adjective ([안 + Verb])
Short-term temporal adverb ('a little later today'); strictly within the same day, contrasting with 나중에 (general/distant future).
Sightseeing/browsing verb; takes place or spectacle with accusative -을/를 (시장을 구경하다, 경기를 구경하다).
Simultaneous action connective suffix ('while doing X'); requires identical subject in both clauses. Vowel/ㄹ stem takes -면서, consonant takes -으면서.
Sino-Korean academic/administrative noun (登錄 = registration / enrollment); forms verbal noun 등록하다; collocations include 수강 등록 (course registration), 등록 기간 (enrollment period).
Sino-Korean age classifier noun (歲 = years of age); requires Sino-Korean numerals (20세 = 이십 세, 만 19세); contrast with pure Korean age counter 살 (스무 살).
Sino-Korean annual frequency adverb (每年 = every year / annually); synonym 해마다; collocations: 매년 봄에 (every spring), 매년 증가하다 (increase every year).
Sino-Korean arrival verb (到着); takes destination goal with -에 (서울역에 도착하다). Antonym of 출발하다.
Sino-Korean base numeral 10,000 (萬); base for the myriad counting system.
Sino-Korean celebration verb (祝賀); takes occasion with -을/를 (생일을 축하하다). Humble form is 축하드리다.

Sino-Korean ceremonial event noun (結婚式 = wedding ceremony / marriage service); collocations: 결혼식에 가다 / 참석하다 (attend a wedding), 결혼식을 올리다 / 하다 (hold a wedding ceremony), 결혼식장 (wedding hall), 결혼식 청첩장 (wedding invitation).
Sino-Korean cognitive noun (經驗 = lived experience / empirical knowledge); collocations: 경험을 쌓다 (accumulate experience), 좋은 경험이 되다, 경험이 풍부하다; forms transitive 경험하다.
Sino-Korean collective noun (兄弟) for brothers/siblings; counter is 명 (형제가 몇 명이에요?).
Sino-Korean cuisine category (韓食); contrasts with 중식 (Chinese), 일식 (Japanese), 양식 (Western).
Sino-Korean cultural noun (文化 = culture); collocations: 한국 문화 (Korean culture), 문화를 체험하다 / 배우다 (experience/learn culture), 문화 차이 (cultural difference), 전통문화 (traditional culture).
Sino-Korean day counter for calendar dates (e.g. 15일). Homonym with 일 (noun: work, number: 1).
Sino-Korean departure verb (出發); takes origin station with -에서 (서울역에서 출발하다). Antonym of 도착하다.
Sino-Korean duration counter for months (個月 = counter for number of months); pairs with Sino-Korean numerals (1개월 [일개월], 3개월 [삼개월], 6개월 [육개월]); contrasts with native month counter 달 (한 달, 두 달).
Sino-Korean hobby predicate (讀書 + 하다); formal phrasing for reading books, contrasting with 책을 읽다.
Sino-Korean intransitive verbal noun (通話하다 = speak on telephone); argument frame: [Person]와/과 통화하다 (친구와 통화하다); 통화 중이다 (line is busy).
Sino-Korean month counter (1월~12월). Irregular drop of batchim: 6월 is 유월 (not 육월), 10월 is 시월 (not 십월).

Sino-Korean noun (事 = work / business / job / matter / event); collocations: 일을 하다 (to work / do a task), 일이 많다 / 바쁘다 (have lots of work), 할 일 (things to do / task), 일이 생기다 (something came up / a situation arose), 무슨 일이에요? (what's going on? / what is the matter?); particle: 일 때문에 (because of work/matter); homonym: distinct from Sino-Korean numeral 일 (1) and day noun 일 (日).
Sino-Korean numeral 1,000 (千); homonym with cloth/fabric (천).
Sino-Korean numeral 100 (百); precedes Sino-Korean measure words (백 원, 백 명).
Sino-Korean numeral 100,000; pronounced [심만] via nasalization (비음화).
Sino-Korean numeral: pairs with Sino-Korean counters (분, 월, 일, 년, 원, 층, 쪽)
Sino-Korean preparation verb (準備); takes direct object with -을/를 (선물/파티/시험을 준비하다).
Sino-Korean reservation verb (豫約); collocates with rooms, hotels, restaurants, tables, appointments. Contrasts with ticket booking 예매하다.
Sino-Korean social noun (約束); collocates with 하다 (make appointment), 있다/없다, 지키다 (keep), 어기다 (break).
Sino-Korean term (今年) for 'this year'; formal counterpart of 올해. Can take time particle -에 (금년에).
Sino-Korean term (來年) for 'next year'; takes time particle -에 (내년에). Future tense concord.
Sino-Korean transitive verb (檢索하다 = search / look up on Internet/database); accusative -을/를 (인터넷에서 단어를 검색하다, 정보를 검색하다).
Sino-Korean transitive verb (署名하다 = sign / affix signature); takes accusative -을/를 (서류에 서명하다, 여기에 서명해 주세요); synonym 사인하다.
Sino-Korean transitive verb (錄音하다 = record sound / voice); accusative -을/를 (목소리를 녹음하다, 음성 녹음); contrast with 녹화하다 (record video).
Sino-Korean verbal noun (外出 = outing / going out of the house); forms intransitive 외출하다; collocations: 외출 준비, 외출 중 (temporarily out of office/home).
Sino-Korean verbal noun (工夫 = study / studying / learning); collocations: 공부를 하다 (transitive: to study; 한국어/시험 공부), 공부가 잘되다, 열공 (slang for studying hard); verbal form 공부하다.
Sino-Korean verbal noun (選擇 = choice / selection / option); forms transitive 선택하다 (to choose / select; 메뉴/진로를 선택하다); antonym 포기.
Sino-Korean week unit; takes Sino-Korean numbers for week durations (일 주일, 2주).
Sino-Korean weekly frequency adverb (每週 = every week / weekly); synonym 주마다; collocations: 매주 주말에 (every weekend), 매주 월요일 (every Monday).

Sino-Korean year counter / noun (年 = year / counter for years); pairs with Sino-Korean numerals (1년 [일년], 2년 [이년], 10년 [십년]); collocations: 2026년 (year 2026), 1년 동안 (for one year), 3학년 (3rd grade/year).
Skill verb ('to be good at'); written as single word (잘하다), contrasting with compound adverbial 잘 하다 ('to do well/nicely'). Antonym is 못하다.
Snack loanword; strongly collocates with movie theaters (영화관에서 팝콘을 먹다) and 먹다.
Snack/cookie noun; counters are 개 (piece) and 봉지 (bag). Collocates with 먹다.
Sneakers/running shoes; pair counter is 켤레. Strictly takes footwear verb 신다 (운동화를 신다).
Snowman compound noun (눈 + 사람); strictly collocates with creation verb 만들다 (눈사람을 만들다).
Social correspondence noun (招待狀 = written invitation / invitation card); counter: 장; collocates with 초대장을 보내다/받다.
Social event loanword; collocates with 하다, 열다 (host party), and 초대하다 (invite to party).
Social gathering compound (送別會 = farewell party / send-off party); collocates with 송별회를 열다/하다; antonym is 환영회.
Social gathering noun ('after-party / celebration after main event'); collocates with 뒤풀이에 가다/참석하다, 공연 뒤풀이.
Social gathering noun (모이다 + ㅁ = meeting / get-together); collocates with 모임을 갖다/하다, 가족 모임; locative -에 가다.
Social hierarchy noun (先輩 = school or workplace senior); addressed politely as 선배님; antonym is 후배 (後輩).
Social manner adverb (together / along with); coljection with comitative particles [Noun]와/과 함께 or [Noun](이)랑 함께 (가족과 함께 여행하다); synonym 같이.

Social manner adverb / nominal adverb (혼자 = alone / by oneself / solo); modifies action verbs (혼자 살다 = live alone, 혼자 밥을 먹다 = eat alone, 혼자 가다); particle attachment 혼자서 (alone by oneself, agentive focus).
Social party compound (歡迎會 = welcoming party / reception); collocates with 신입생 환영회, 환영회를 열다.
Social petition noun (付託 = request / favor); collocates with 부탁을 하다/받다, 부탁을 들어주다, 잘 부탁드립니다.
Social relation verb: (1) make friends (친구를 사귀다), (2) date someone (남자친구를 사귀다 / OO와 사귀다).
Social reunion noun (同窓會 = alumni reunion / class gathering); collocates with 동창회에 가다/참석하다.
Social verb (招待 + 하다 = to invite someone); takes person with -을/를 and destination with -에 (친구를 집에 초대하다).
Societal age/status noun (adult / grown-up / elder); commands honorific address and deferential speech; collocations: 어른들께 인사하다, 어른이 되다; antonym 아이 / 어린이.
Societal/existential noun (世上 = world / society / life); collocates with 세상에 태어나다, 세상에서 제일.
Sociocultural conduct noun (禮節 = etiquette / propriety / manners); collocations: 예절을 지키다 (mind one's manners), 식사 예절 (table etiquette), 기본 예절.
Sociolinguistic relational noun (아래 + 사람 = junior / subordinate / younger person); receives plain/informal speech (반말/하대); antonym 윗사람 (superior/elder).
Sociolinguistic relational noun (위 + 사람 = superior / senior / elder); requires honorific language (존댓말), honorific particles (-께, -께서), and polite bow; antonym 아랫사람 (junior).
Socks noun; counter is 켤레. Strictly takes footwear verb 신다 (양말을 신다) and 벗다.

Somatic injury verb (to get hurt / be injured); body part takes accusative -을/를 (팔/다리/허리를 다치다); stem 다치- -> 다쳐요 / 다쳐서; adverbial 크게 다치다 (be badly hurt).
Spa/geothermal noun (溫泉 = hot spring); collocates with 온천에 가다, 온천욕.
Spatial adverb derived from 멀다 (far / far away / distantly); modifies motion/location verbs (멀리 가다, 멀리 보다, 멀리서 오다); antonym 가까이.
Spatial compound noun (여기 + 저기); takes locative -에, accusative -을/를 (여기저기를 구경하다), or functions adverbially.
Spatial noun (位置 = location / geographic position); collocates with 위치를 확인하다 / 찾다 (check/find location), 위치가 좋다 (good location).

Spatial relational noun (outside / the open air / outdoors); locative 바깥에 (outdoors / outside); antonym 안 (inside); collocations: 바깥 날씨, 바깥 공기.
Spatial/temporal adverb derived from 가깝다 (close by / nearby / nearly); modifies motion or position verbs (가까이 오다, 가까이 살다); also nearly/approximately with numbers (100명 가까이).
Special-interest club noun (同好會 = hobby/interest club); collocates with 등산 동호회, 동호회에 가입하다.
Speed/urgency manner adverb ('quickly / hurry'); antonym of 천천히. Modifies actions (빨리 오다, 빨리 걷다).
Spelled 며칠 (etymologically not 몇 일). Interrogative for calendar date: pairs with 몇 월 (몇 월 며칠이에요?).
Spontaneous emotive interjection ('ah / oh / alas'); expresses realization, surprise, or sudden remembrance (아, 그렇군요!, 아, 맞다).

Sport loanword noun (bowling); paired with verb 치다 (볼링을 치다 = play bowling); locative 볼링장 (bowling alley), 볼링공 (bowling ball).
Sports action verb: paired with racket and ball sports taking accusative -을/를 (테니스/골프/탁구/볼링을 치다); conjugates 쳐요 / 쳐서 / 칩니다.
Sports facility noun; takes locative -에서 (골프장에서 골프를 치다).
Sports facility noun; takes locative -에서 (탁구장에서 탁구를 치다).
Sports venue noun; takes locative -에서 (농구장에서 농구를 하다).
Sports venue noun; takes locative -에서 (테니스장에서 테니스를 치다).
Sports venue; takes locative -에서 (수영장에서 수영하다) or directional -에 가다.

Sportswear noun (水泳服 = swimsuit / swimwear); selectional restriction: takes wearable verb 입다 (수영복을 입다/벗다).
Spreading/unfolding verb ('to open / unfold / spread / straighten'); takes object with -을/를 (책을 펴다, 우산을 펴다, 어깨를 펴다); antonym is 접다 / 덮다.
Spring blossom noun; collocates with seasonal festival 봄, verb 피다 (벚꽃이 피다), and 구경하다.
Spring season noun; takes time particle -에 (봄에). Collocates with 따뜻하다 and 꽃이 피다.
State/emotion adjective (幸福하다 = happy / blissful); antonym is 불행하다; nominal form is 행복.
Story/conversation noun; contracts colloquially to 얘기. Forms intransitive verb with -하다 (이야기하다 / 얘기하다).
Subject honorific pre-final suffix (선어말어미); honors the subject of the clause. Vowel stem takes -시-, consonant stem takes -으시- (가시다, 읽으시다).

Substance noun (材料 = ingredients / raw materials); collocates with 요리 재료, 건축 재료; 재료를 준비하다.

Sufficiency construction: verb stem + -(으)면 되다 ('all one needs to do is / it is enough to / fine if'); consonant takes -으면 되다, vowel/ㄹ takes -면 되다 (여기서 기다리면 돼요, 이것만 사면 돼요).
Summer beach recreation VP (海水浴場 + 에 가다); seasonal summer collocation with 수영하다.
Summer season noun; takes time particle -에 (여름에). Collocates with 덥다 and 여름방학/여름휴가.
Superlative adverb (第一); synonym of native Korean 가장. Modifies adjectives (제일 크다) or verbs (제일 좋아하다).
Superlative evaluation noun and modifier (最高 = the best / highest / maximum); collocations: 오늘 최고 기온 (today's high temperature), 기분이 최고다, 최고 기록; antonym 최저 (最低).
Superlative measurement noun and modifier (最低 = lowest / minimum); collocations: 오늘 최저 기온 (today's low temperature), 최저 임금 (minimum wage); antonym 최고 (最高).

Suppletive humble verb for 주다; takes honorific dative -께 (선생님께 드리다). Functions as humble benefactive auxiliary -어/아 드리다.
Suppletive subject honorific for both 먹다 and 마시다. Collocates with honorific food noun 진지 (진지를 드시다) or beverages.
Suppletive subject honorific for 자다; formulaic bedtime greeting: 안녕히 주무세요.
Suppletive subject honorific of existence for persons (선생님께서 계시다); contrasts with 있으시다 (used for attributes/possessions of honored person).
Symptom noun (cough); collocations: 기침을 하다 (to cough), 기침이 나다 / 멈추다 (cough occurs / stops), 심한 기침 (severe cough).
Symptom noun (코 + 물 = nasal mucus / runny nose); collocations: 콧물이 나다 / 흐르다 (have a runny nose), 콧물을 풀다 (blow one's nose), 콧물 감기 (head cold).
Symptom noun (頭痛 = headache); collocations: 두통이 있다 / 심하다, 두통약을 먹다 (take headache medicine), 편두통 (migraine).
Tactile temperature adjective (hot to the touch / boiling); applied to objects, liquids, and food (뜨거운 물, 국물이 뜨겁다); contrast with 덥다 (weather/climate); b-irregular (뜨거워요 / 뜨거워서 / 뜨거우면 / 뜨거운).

Taste attribute noun: pairs with 있다/없다 (맛이 있다/없다)
Telephone greeting formula ('Hello?'); strictly conventionalized for answering or checking caller line on phone.
Temporal abstract noun (未來 = the future); antonyms 과거 (past) and 현재 (present); collocations: 밝은 미래 (bright future), 미래를 준비하다.
Temporal abstract noun (過去 = the past / bygone days); antonyms 현재 (present) and 미래 (future); grammatical past tense is 과거형 / 과거시제.
Temporal achievement adverb ('finally / at last / in the end'); signals long-awaited outcome (드디어 끝났다, 드디어 만났다).
Temporal adverb ('early'); antonym of 늦게. Modifies action verbs (일찍 일어나다, 일찍 자다, 일찍 오다).
Temporal adverb (a little while ago / earlier today); strictly refers to past events within the same day; antonym 이따가 / 나중에 (later today); collocations: 아까 본 사람.
Temporal adverb (今方 = momentarily / in a second / shortly; or just now); collocations: 금방 돌아올게요 (I will be right back), 금방 끝나다.
Temporal adverb and noun (暫時 = a short while / briefly / for a moment); polite requests: 잠시만 기다려 주세요 (please wait a moment); synonym 잠깐.
Temporal and spatial passage verb ('to pass by / elapse / exceed'); takes elapsed time as subject (시간이 지나다, 1년이 지났다) or spatial transit (신촌을 지나다).

Temporal aspect adverb (이제 = now / from now on / at this point); indicates contrast with previous state or commencement of new phase: 이제 가야 해요 (I must go now), 이제 시작합니다; distinct from 지금 (neutral objective right now).
Temporal clause construction ('when / at the time of doing/being'); attaches to verb/adjective stems via -(으)ㄹ; can take past marker -았/었을 때 for completed prior states.
Temporal compound noun (지난 + 번 = last time / previous occasion / the other day); collocations: 지난번에 (last time; 지난번에 이야기한 것), 지난번 시험.
Temporal compound noun (年末 = year-end / close of the year); collocations: 연말연시 (year-end and new year), 연말 모임 (year-end gathering); antonym 연초 (年始).

Temporal duration adverb ('for a long time'); collocates with duration verbs (오래 기다리다, 오래 걸리다, 오래 살다).
Temporal duration connective clause ('during the time that / while'); verb stem + -는 동안 (내가 자는 동안, 한국에 있는 동안); with nouns, simply noun + 동안 (방학 동안, 세 시간 동안).
Temporal duration noun (期間 = period / duration / term); collocates with 방학 기간, 유효 기간 (expiration period), 신청 기간.

Temporal noun and adverb (現在 = the present / currently / as of now); antonyms 과거 (past) and 미래 (future); collocations: 현재 시각 (current time), 현재 위치 (current position).

Temporal noun/adverb ('these days / lately'); functions adverbially without particle or takes -에. Present-tense concord.
Temporal phrase (학기 + 中); indicates duration while semester is in session. Takes time particle -에 (학기 중에).
Temporal posterior sequence connective (-(으)ㄴ 뒤에 = 'after doing X'); vowel/ㄹ takes -ㄴ 뒤에 (졸업한 뒤에, 운동한 뒤에), consonant takes -은 뒤에 (밥을 먹은 뒤에); synonyms -(으)ㄴ 후에 / -(으)ㄴ 다음에.

Temporal relation noun / bound noun (前 = before / ago / prior to); attaches after time quantities (3년 전 = 3 years ago, 며칠 전 = a few days ago) or action nominals / verbs (-기 전에 = before doing X: 밥 먹기 전에); antonym 후 (後 = after).
Temporal relational noun (後 = after / later); follows nouns or clauses (식사 후, 퇴근 후, [Time] 후에, -(으)ㄴ 후에 = after doing).

Temporal/sequential adverb ('first / in advance'); contrasts with 나중에 (later) or 그 다음에 (after that).
Temporal/spatial precision adverb ('directly / immediately / right away / none other than'); modifies verbs or nouns (바로 가다, 바로 지금, 바로 그 사람).
Tentative intention/deliberative construction: verb stem + -(으)ㄹ까 하다 ('thinking of doing / considering'); restricted to 1st person subject in statements (유학을 갈까 해요, 차를 바꿀까 해요).
Terminal order noun ('the last / final'); modifies following noun directly or with possessive (마지막 날, 마지막 기회); antonym is 처음 / 첫.

Third-person volition auxiliary predicate (-고 싶어하다 = 'subject wants to do X'); attaches to Action verb stems (친구가 한국에 가고 싶어해요); marks direct objects with -을/를 (한국어를 배우고 싶어해요); distinct from 1st/2nd person -고 싶다.

Toiletry noun ('soap'); counter: 개; collocates with 비누로 손을 씻다, 비누칠하다.

Tourism compound noun (國內旅行 = domestic travel); antonym 해외여행 (international travel); collocations: 국내 여행을 다니다.
Tourism compound noun (團體觀光 = group package tour / party sightseeing); collocations: 단체 관광객 (group tourists), 단체 관광 버스.

Tourism compound noun (海外旅行 = overseas travel / international trip); antonym 국내 여행; collocations: 해외여행을 떠나다, 여권과 해외여행.
Tourism compound noun (背囊旅行 = backpacking trip / budget independent travel); collocations: 유럽 배낭여행을 떠나다 (go backpacking in Europe).
Tourism compound noun (自由旅行 = independent travel / self-guided tour); antonym 패키지 여행 (packaged tour); collocations: 자유 여행 상품.
Tourism destination noun (旅行地 = travel destination / vacation spot); collocations: 인기 여행지 (popular tourist spot), 국내/해외 여행지, 여행지를 추천하다.
Tourism noun (觀光地 = tourist spot / sightseeing attraction); collocates with 유명한 관광지, 둘러보다.
Traction/depression verb ('to press / push down / suppress'); 르-irregular: 눌러요 / 눌러서; takes button/bell with -을/를 (버튼/벨을 누르다, 번호를 누르다).
Trading firm workplace (貿易會社); takes allative -에 with 다니다.

Traditional culinary dish noun (雜菜 = stir-fried glass noodles with vegetables and beef); prepared for festive occasions; counter: 접시.
Traditional culinary noun ('rice cake'); collocates with 떡을 빚다/찌다/치다/먹다; counter: 개, 말, 되.
Traditional culinary noun (된醬 = fermented soybean paste); collocates with 된장찌개, 된장을 풀다.
Traditional floor cushion noun (方席 = sitting mat/cushion); collocates with 방석을 깔다 (spread/place cushion), 방석에 앉다; counter: 장 or 개.
Traditional formal New Year bow to elders (歲拜 + 하다); takes recipient with honorific -께 (할아버지께 세배하다). Recipient gives 세뱃돈.

Transit directional noun (直進 = going straight / proceeding forward); collocates with 직진하다, 직진 신호.

Transit itinerary noun (片道 = one-way trip / single journey); antonym 왕복 (round-trip); collocations: 편도 표 / 항공권 (one-way ticket), 편도 1시간.
Transit loanword noun ('U-turn'); collocates with 유턴하다, 유턴 구역.

Transit station noun (昇降場 = railway/subway boarding platform); locative -에서 (승강장에서 기다리다).
